_directions.a: Recommended default, written into each fragment: plain, warm, one felt moment, third person for Dr San.
_directions.b: Plain and few: the shortest honest version of each line. Empty strings hide a line.
_directions.c: In her words: Dr San speaks in the first person, drawing on her own lines (map, test, build, practise; 'no interest in becoming one').
_directions.d: Warmer and more direct: conversational, answers the question a reader would actually ask.

b.h1: Retiring soon? Here’s how we’d plan it together.

c.h1: I help you plan who you’ll be when work stops.
c.lede: Human-centred retirement planning™, for your psychological and social wellbeing. On your own or as a couple.

d.h1: The date is set. What about the Monday after?
d.lede: We’ll plan it together, alongside the financial plan you already have.

b.l1: A cake. A card. A speech.
b.l2: No alarm. A very quiet house.

c.l1: The cake, the card, the speech. Everyone tells you to enjoy it.
c.l2: The alarm doesn’t go off. The coffee is lovely. The house is very quiet.
c.l3: No one needs you anywhere today. The phone hasn’t rung since Friday.
c.close: That isn’t a failing. It’s a change nobody planned for, and it can be.

d.h: What the first week can feel like.
d.l1: Cake, a card, a speech, and a lot of people telling you you’ve earned it.
d.l2: You sleep in. It’s lovely. By lunchtime the house feels very big.
d.l3: Nobody needs anything from you. You check your phone more than you’d like to admit.
d.close: That’s normal, and it’s fixable. It just needs a plan of its own.

b.lede: Four stages. You always know where you are.
b.s1p: What does work give you now? We write it down.
b.s2p: We try a week without it and see what’s missing.
b.s3p: We plan what fills each gap.
b.s4p: You try it before you finish work, and we adjust.

c.lede: You map what work is actually doing for you, test what happens when it stops, then build the replacements and practise them.
c.s1p: We start with what your work is quietly doing for you: the routine, the identity, the purpose, the people.
c.s1o: You’ll see exactly what leaves with the job.
c.s2p: We test what happens when it stops, before it actually does.
c.s2o: You’ll know where the gaps are.
c.s3p: We build the replacements: real things, in your own community, that suit you.
c.s3o: You’ll have a plan for your weeks.
c.s4p: You practise them while you still have somewhere to be on Monday.
c.s4o: By your last day, they’re already part of your week.
c.note: If you have a partner, bring them. I’m very happy to work with couples.

d.h: Here’s what happens, step by step.
d.lede: Good conversations, and a plan you can actually use.
d.s1p: We talk about what a normal work week gives you, beyond the pay.
d.s1o: You’ll see what’s really at stake.
d.s2p: We picture the week without it, then try a few days of it for real.
d.s3p: We choose what goes back in: people, purpose, a reason to get going.
d.s3o: A week worth waking up for.
d.s4p: You try the new routine now, while it’s low stakes, and we fine-tune it.
d.note: Coming as a couple? Even better. You’ll be sharing those weeks.

b.i2p: On your own or with your partner.

c.lede: You don’t need to prepare anything. Just bring the date, and whatever’s on your mind.
c.i1p: Thirty minutes, at no cost, so we can see whether I’m the right fit for you.
c.i2p: Just you and me, or you, your partner and me, working through the four stages.
c.i3p: Everything we work out, written down in plain words for you to keep.
c.i4p: I’ll check in as your date gets closer, so the plan keeps up with your life.

d.lede: Straightforward, no jargon, and at a pace that suits you.
d.i1p: Thirty free minutes to talk it through and ask anything.
d.i2p: Sessions with Dr San, just you or both of you.
d.i3t: A plan you can stick on the fridge
d.i3p: Short, clear and yours. Not a report that sits in a drawer.
d.i4p: Check-ins as the date gets closer.

b.a1: No. It sits alongside your financial plan.
b.a3: Three to ten years out is easiest. Any time is fine.

c.h: Questions you might have for me.
c.a1: No. I’m not a financial adviser, and I have no interest in becoming one. I help with the other half of the plan.
c.a2: No. It’s education: practical planning for your days, your people and your purpose. If something bigger comes up, I’ll help you find the right support.
c.a3: Three to ten years out is ideal, while you still have time, colleagues and energy. But I’m happy to talk whenever you’re ready.
c.a4: Yes, please do. Two people retiring into one house is well worth planning for together.
c.a5: Not at all. I work by video wherever you are, and in person around Cairns.
c.a6: The first 30-minute chat is free. I’ll talk you through the rest then, with no pressure either way.

d.q1: Isn’t this what my financial planner does?
d.a1: Not quite. Your planner makes sure the money lasts. This makes sure the days are worth it. The two work well together.
d.a2: No. It’s practical planning, done with care. If you need a different kind of support, Dr San will help you find it.
d.q3: Am I too early? Too late?
d.a3: Probably neither. Three to ten years out is the easiest time, but it’s never too late to start.
d.q4: My partner retires at a different time. Does that matter?
d.a4: Not at all. Come together or separately. Planning around two different dates is part of the work.
d.a5: Far North Queensland. Sessions run by video anywhere, and in person around Cairns.
d.a6: The first chat is free. After that, Dr San will be upfront about cost before anything is booked.

c.h: I’d love to hear from you.
c.lede: Book a friendly 30-minute chat with me. We’ll talk about what your weeks might look like.

d.lede: Thirty minutes, free, and no pressure either way.
